chapter_seo_title: Desolate Era Chapter 471: Ji Ning vs Ten Thousand Blood-Eyed Warriors
chapter_meta_description: The Broken Horn World throws a deadly swarm at Ji Ning. Can his sword-art and Eight-Nine Arcane Art hold out against an alien war machine built for attrition?
og_title: Desolate Era Ch. 471 – A Sword Against Ten Thousand
og_description: Ji Ning literally tanks a swarm of ten thousand enemies while conserving his divine power. But the real threat hasn't even moved yet.
twitter_description: Ji Ning vs. an alien army that spawns from mouths. Sword-art, soul-tanking, and a cold tactical calculation.

lore_anchors.definition: The supreme protective divine ability beneath the True God level, granting physical indestructibility that makes the cultivator's body comparable to a magic treasure, allowing them to tank blows without injury.

A sacred Fiendgod divine ability that allows the user to swell to a towering thousand-zhang form, amplifying strength and speed proportionally. Not mere gigantification—it channels the density of the cosmos into the body.
A legendary Fiendgod battle form where the cultivator grows additional heads and limbs, multiplying close-combat offensive and defensive coverage exponentially.
A soul-hardening cultivation state where the mind becomes as unyielding as frozen ice, providing immense resistance to mental and soul-based attacks.
A top-tier wind-element movement divine ability used by Ji Ning for extreme burst speed.
An invisible, inescapable wave of mental force that bypasses physical defenses and targets the enemy's soul directly. The blood-eyed warriors specialize in this form of warfare.

A top-ten divine ability of the Three Realms, created by Daoist Threelives, that hardens the user's hands into ultimate weapons capable of crushing stars. Extremely powerful but consumes vast amounts of divine power.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn't Ji Ning just use Starseizing Hand to clear the swarm faster?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Starseizing Hand consumes enormous divine power per use. Ji Ning is conserving his reserves because he knows the real enemies—the black-cloaked warriors and their commander—have not yet joined the fight in earnest. Burning fuel on fodder would leave him helpless.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the ten thousand blood-eyed warriors die so easily?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They are cannon fodder—mass-produced spawns with no "undying body" ability. Each is roughly at the Void Fiendgod level of strength but cannot regenerate. Once decapitated or bisected, they die permanently.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the curved-horn warriors laugh while watching Ji Ning kill their spawn?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The blood-eyed warriors are expendable. Each curved-horn warrior can control a limited number of spawn, so they actually *need* the cannon fodder to die before they can hatch more. Ji Ning's massacre was doing them a favor in replenishment terms.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the "Iceheart Realm" and why is it important here?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Iceheart Realm is a soul-hardening technique that grants near-perfect resistance to mental attacks. When 5,000 blood-eyed warriors launched a coordinated soul-assault, Ji Ning's Iceheart cultivation allowed him to withstand it without flinching—a silent demonstration of his soul's toughness.
